title: POC scoping: model tradeoffs & benchmarks — Sundial Energy
summary: POC scoping for Sundial Energy: define success criteria (latency, throughput, accuracy), workload size, multilingual needs (ES/PT/DE), shortlist open models and quantization options, agree benchmarks and 3-week timeline for pilot. Security docs and sample dataset to be shared.
next_steps: Jordan to send POC pricing estimate and redwood security packet (SOC2/SAML/KMS) by 2026-12-10
Maya to run baseline benchmark on 3 shortlisted models with Sundial sample by 2026-12-14
Sundial (Carlos) to upload ~5k sample tickets + 10k short doc snippets to S3 link by 2026-12-09
Schedule follow-up bench review for week of 2026-12-15
action_items: Jordan - send pricing and compliance docs; due 2026-12-10
Maya - baseline runs (models: m3-small, amphora-v1, gemini-open-lite) and initial latency/cost numbers; due 2026-12-14
Carlos - provide sanitized sample dataset + acceptance criteria doc; due 2026-12-09
Lukas - confirm VPC peering window and security contacts; due 2026-12-11
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — looks like we're all here. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Carlos: Carlos here, Head of ML at Sundial.
[00:08] Aisha: Aisha, platform lead.
[00:10] Lukas: Lukas, CTO.
[00:12] Nora: Nora, data scientist.
[00:14] Jordan: Great. Maya from Redwood is on the call — Maya, do you want to intro the bench plan?
[00:20] Maya: Sure, thanks Jordan. Hi all — quick context: we're scoped for a 3-week pilot, typical POC objectives are to validate latency & cost at your expected load, verify quality on your domain prompts (work orders, fault reports), and confirm multilingual handling for Spanish and Portuguese, and some German.
[00:36] Nora: Yep that's right. We also have lots of short telemetry notes — like 35-100 tokens typically. Some followup emails are longer, 200-400 tokens.
[00:46] Jordan: Perfect, good to know. Carlos, can you share success criteria top-level? What would make this a win for Sundial?
[00:51] Carlos: Primary is accuracy on entity extraction and intent routing — F1 we'd like >0.85 on critical intents. Sec is after that: latency end-to-end under 250ms p95 for single-turn classification calls, and cost per 1k predictions below a threshold — we have a target but we'll give numbers after this call. Multilingual is must-have for ES/PT; German is lower priority but nice to have.
[01:12] Maya: Understood. On latency, quick note — hosted versus dedicated will change the numbers. For hosted we can usually get sub-200ms p95 on trimmed models but costs are higher; dedicated/reserved would reduce tail but requires commit.
[01:25] Aisha: We're leaning away from a big commit initially — want to validate before Reserved. Also curious about on-prem / VPC options for later.
[01:33] Jordan: Totally reasonable. We'll scope a hosted pilot first with VPC peering option.
[01:37] Lukas: Security wise, we need SOC2 + SSO/SAML, audit logs and KMS integration for keys on any private deployments. Also need proof of data retention policies.
[01:46] Ethan: We'll include the security packet; SOC2 and SSO are standard. KMS for Private is available, we can also do customer-managed keys for Dedicated.
[01:54] Nora: For workload sizing: our expected steady throughput is ~40-60 requests per second during peak 9-6, with spikes up to 120 rps for short windows. Avg tokens per request ~120, embeddings usage sporadic — about 1 embedding per 3 requests for rerank.
[02:09] Maya: Good details. So for benchmarking we'll simulate steady 60 rps and a 120 rps spike scenario. We'll also run per-request latency and token-cost profiling.
[02:17] Carlos: On models — we've been looking at open models to avoid vendor lock, but quality tradeoffs are the big concern. What would you recommend for initial shortlist?
[02:26] Maya: Given your constraints (short inputs, classification/extraction, multilingual ES/PT) I'd suggest a balanced shortlist: 1) m3-small (Llama-3 family style) for lowest-latency, good zero-shot; 2) amphora-v1 (a mid-size model that tends to handle multilingual better); 3) gemma-open-lite (strong on code & structured extraction) — note these names are placeholders for the actual model builds we'll test. We'll also test a quantized 4-bit variant where applicable.
[02:50] Carlos: Can we see tradeoffs in quality vs cost? For instance, if amphora-v1 is 10% better but 2x cost, that might be worth it for critical paths.
[02:58] Maya: Absolutely — the bench will produce per-model precision/recall, latency p50/p95, and cost per 1k calls. We'll provide a decision matrix.
[03:06] Aisha: Do you support KV cache and prefix caching for short repeated prompts? We have a lot of repetitive status checks.
[03:12] Maya: Yes, Redwood runtime supports prefix and KV cache; I'll note that caching will materially reduce cost for repeated sequences. The transcription sometimes calls it "kay-v cache" but it's KV memory.
[03:20] Nora: How about domain adaptation? Fine-tuning vs prompt engineering?
[03:23] Maya: For the POC we recommend prompt engineering + few-shot examples and local context windows. Fine-tuning is possible but longer; we can simulate instruction tuning via retrieval-augmented prompts and early adaptation. If results are poor, we can discuss local fine-tune in a later phase.
[03:36] Jordan: Timeline check: we want to do the baseline runs and reconvene within two weeks. Is that feasible?
[03:40] Maya: Yes — if we get the sample dataset by Dec 9, we can run baseline and have initial results by Dec 14, then review week of Dec 15. That matches the 3-week pilot kickoff if you want to start right after review.
[03:51] Carlos: Sounds good. One question: do you have metrics for hallucination or confidence scoring? For extraction we need low false positives.
[03:58] Maya: We'll include an extraction precision metric and a confidence-calibrated threshold analysis. Also we can include a small human-eval set for critical intents.
[04:07] Lukas: Network: what's required for VPC peering? We have a strict egress rule; want to minimize data touch.
[04:12] Ethan: We'll request VPC peering info and a one-way egress plan. For hosted pilot, you can restrict data ingress to a presigned S3 or use private peering; full Private deployment is an option later.
[04:22] Nora: Any competitor notes? We tested internal self-hosting with optimized quantization but management overhead killed velocity. Also experimented with OpenAI endpoints, good quality but cost and residency were issues.
[04:33] Maya: That mirrors what we usually hear. We'll benchmark against the open models and provide a rough comparison to managed endpoints to highlight cost/latency tradeoffs.
[04:41] Jordan: Let's talk acceptance criteria for the POC: 1) extraction F1 >=0.85 on critical intents, 2) p95 latency <250ms in steady 60 rps, 3) cost <= your internal threshold — Carlos will provide number, 4) multilingual parity: ES within 5% of EN baseline. Agree?
[04:56] Carlos: Yes, add stability — no major errors or timeouts during 120 rps spike test.
[05:01] Maya: Noted. For the benchmark runs I'll produce: per-model CSV with fields: model, quantization, p50, p95 latency, tokens per call, cost per 1k, precision, recall, F1, hallucination rate.
[05:15] Nora: Do you include token-fine breakdowns? We need to know prompt vs completion token counts per call.
[05:19] Maya: Yes we'll break down token counts and show where costs are coming from. If you have long system prompts we can optimize that too.
[05:25] Carlos: About multilingual: our Spanish region uses many colloquialisms; will you include locale-specific testcases?
[05:30] Maya: Please include a small set of real Spanish/Portuguese examples in the sample data; we'll flag mis-transcriptions in results.
[05:36] Lukas: For deployment paths — after POC what's the typical ramp? We might go to Dedicated for stable savings.
[05:42] Jordan: Many customers do Hosted pilot -> Dedicated reserved if committed throughput makes sense. We'll model cost at your steady 60 rps to estimate break-even.
[05:49] Aisha: Anything else on security? We need a SOC2 attestation and a named contact for audits.
[05:54] Ethan: I'll attach the SOC2 report and list of contacts in the security packet.
[05:58] Nora: Minor transcription note — sometimes vendor docs mis- name model families. Please include exact model SHA or image tags when you send the bench results so we can reproduce.
[06:06] Maya: Absolutely — we'll include image tags/commit hashes for each model run along with env specs and quantization flags.
[06:12] Jordan: Alright let's wrap with explicit next steps. Jordan send pricing & security packet by Dec 10. Maya run baseline and share initial results by Dec 14. Carlos provide dataset by Dec 9. Schedule follow-up for Dec 15-17. Anything to add?
[06:26] Carlos: No, that's all. Thanks everyone.
[06:28] Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with links to the S3 upload and bench template.
[06:34] Aisha: Thanks all.
[06:36] End of recording.

Notes: occasional mis-transcribed acronyms (V-P-C written, "kay-v" for KV), speaker overlap around 03:00, some filler words and run-on sentences preserved. Bench plan to include a canary test and spike test, plus cost model for hosted vs dedicated.
